IIT Mandi Catalyst continued Day 3 of the ongoing 5-Day Advanced Course on MedTech Innovation, Intellectual Property & Patent Strategy, being held from 12–16 October 2026.

💡 𝐒𝐞𝐬𝐬𝐢𝐨𝐧 𝟑: At the Interface of Medicine, Engineering and IP – Strategies for MedTech Innovation and Patent Protection

The session was led by Mr. B. Saha (Aditya), Co-Founder, Bizrights IP Partners.
The session explored fundamental concepts of intellectual property through real-world examples and practical insights. Participants learned to distinguish between discovery, research results, prototypes, inventions, and commercial products. A key takeaway was that owning a patent does not automatically grant the freedom to commercialize an invention.

💡 𝐒𝐞𝐬𝐬𝐢𝐨𝐧 𝟒: IP Management, Technology Transfer & Institutional Innovation Ecosystem
The session was led by Dr. Vinita Jindal, Registered Indian Patent Agent, Deputy General Manager (DGM) and Head – IP & Technology Management, BIRAC.

The session focused on evaluating Invention Disclosure Forms, understanding technology transfer mechanisms, and navigating the journey from innovation to market. Discussions also covered establishing inventorship, determining IP ownership under employment policies and funding agreements, managing pre-existing technologies and confidential information, defining ownership through collaboration agreements, and balancing commercial interests, clinical validation, research publication, and patient welfare to facilitate the successful translation of innovations into impactful healthcare solutions. 

The sessions provided valuable insights into protecting MedTech innovations, managing intellectual property strategically, and translating research outcomes into impactful healthcare solutions.

💡 𝐒𝐞𝐬𝐬𝐢𝐨𝐧 𝟐: Design Thinking for MedTech Innovation – From Problem Identification to Solution Definition

The session was led by Prof. (Dr.) Dipankar Deb, Faculty In-Charge & Director – Incubation, IIT Mandi Catalyst.

💬 𝐊𝐞𝐲 𝐇𝐢𝐠𝐡𝐥𝐢𝐠𝐡𝐭𝐬

Day 2 featured interactive discussions on AI-driven healthcare innovation, patent strategy, and product development. Participants explored key questions, including:
🔹 Can AI-powered search tools help researchers explore and refine their ideas?
🔹 Should a patent be filed before developing an AI model for radiograph interpretation and integration with Electronic Health Records (EHR)?
🔹 What is the pathway from Idea → Patent → Model Development → Validation → CDSCO Regulatory Approval?
🔹 A practical checklist for medical research was also discussed, highlighting important considerations for translating research ideas into innovative healthcare solutions.

The session encouraged participants to think critically about problem identification, intellectual property protection, and the journey from research concepts to validated, market-ready MedTech solutions.

🚀 From Prototype to Market-Ready: Mentoring Startups at IIT Mandi Catalyst

IIT Mandi Catalyst organised an insightful session on Prototype to Market-Ready Development for its incubated startups, led by Mr. Shishir Tewari, Manager – Data Engineering, Procore Technologies.

The session featured startup presentations, product readiness discussions, and technical mentoring, focusing on MVP development, market validation, and a structured framework for achieving market readiness.

B2B or B2C? Your customer decides how you should go to market. 👇

A strong product is only one part of the equation. Your Go-To-Market (GTM) strategy needs to change based on who you're selling to.

In B2B, buying decisions often involve multiple stakeholders, longer evaluation cycles, business value, reliability, and measurable results.

In B2C, the journey is often more direct, with factors such as price, convenience, brand, experience, and customer preference playing a major role.

For startups, understanding this difference can help you make better decisions around:

🔹 Who your real decision-maker is
🔹 What motivates your customer to buy
🔹 Where you should reach them
🔹 How your sales journey should work
🔹 Which metrics actually matter
